origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-badge-vps

Brett (voice): "I need a setting in the Claude badge plugin that has a VPS connection and a console connection, and I need to be able to put them on icons only and select which icons for each one."

Claude badge plugin (apps/console-web/plugins/claude-badge):
1. Two connections, each its own badge/indicator on the banner:
   - Console connection: the existing test (console AI via axf.llm@1).
   - VPS connection: the Claude Code login on the VPS (which account, logged in or not, limit hit). Read it with plain code, zero tokens (e.g. the ai-keys/claude-accounts VPS status or a cheap read of /root/.claude.json email + credentials expiry); green = logged in and working, amber = limit hit / out of credits, gray/red = not logged in.
2. Settings (Settings > Plugins > Claude badge): show/hide each one; Icons only switch per badge; pick the icon for each badge and each state (ok / no credit / error), extending the existing Badge icons picker.
3. Covers step 18 of pending item token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control (clock badge watches VPS login): note it there, don't build it twice.
4. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

Nothing gets removed. One session for the whole build, read only files you need, no full CLAUDE.md chain. Stay out of notes/tasks/todo and AmberX notification code (other builds).
## UPDATE from Brett (replaces the scope above)
"I need the Claude badge, the axHub badge, the VPS badge and the AmberX badge, all in one plugin, all able to select which icon for which, and fully configurable."
- One plugin holds four badges: Claude (console AI), axHub (connection/health), VPS (Claude login on the VPS), AmberX (phone app connected/last seen). Move the existing ones in; old plugins can be disabled, nothing removed.
- Per badge: show/hide, icons only or icon + label, label text, icon per state (ok / warn / error / off), order on the banner.
- All plain-code checks, zero tokens.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
Add a usage meter for the Claude account signed in on the VPS (used out of total, 5-hour and weekly) to the same badge plugin, same options (show/hide, icon only, icons per state). Reuse the existing usage-meter widget code; don't build a second meter. This covers the 'Banner widget: usage meter of the account signed in on the VPS' step of token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control-small-steps; note it there.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"When we click that widget in the banner, it's gonna do whatever we have it set to do. Like, maybe it can drop down and show a list of all the accounts that are in console. It can show how many credits are left for all the accounts that are configured to connect to the VPS."
- Each badge/widget has a configurable tap action (setting): drop-down, open a screen, run a command, toggle, nothing.
- Usage meter default tap = drop-down listing every Claude account saved in the console/VPS: name, type, active marker, credits left (5-hour + weekly, reset time), status. Plain code reads, zero tokens; cached with a refresh button.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md
steps.why: new shared asset types + cross-port contract

steps.text: Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI
steps.why: library format + converter correctness is a contract every port reads

steps.text: Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections
steps.why: first consumer of the icon-library and icon-map contracts; shapes the plugin's data model

steps.text: Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group
steps.why: changes how GUIs work across apps (window / dock engine use, drag-drop between hosts)

steps.text: Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

steps.text: Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library
steps.why: forms and integrations on top of the contracts

steps.text: Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections

steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

before.detail: Fable phase: designer@1 contracts (add-on model, designer + embed asset types, designed@1 manifest + identifier + registration, designer-doc@1 interaction contract, asset-context@1 section), fixtures, validators, checks, PORTING.md, DESIGNER.md. Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). Supersedes the menu / toolbar editors of the old asset-designer pending build.

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

Host plugin skeleton: plugins/ui-asset-designer from _template (id ai.amberx.axf.console.ui-asset-designer, uiEditor builder, lifecycle, install/uninstall, provides service:axf.designer@1), nav Plugins → UI asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab rendered through settings/designer; plugin-lifecycle check passes

Host server (FastAPI): capability axf.designer@1 (addons, library, get, validate, save, register, preview), designer-library@1 index in the lifecycle dataDir, saves through makeDesigned / withDesigned, built-in ids refused, plugin-commands@1 auto routes; test.py

Host web shell: add-on list (designerAddonChoices, installed / missing with a link to the plugin), asset library panel (designed + built-in per type, search, New / Open / Duplicate / Delete), designer interface + settings interface pickers (inherit@1 copies, Reset to default)

Shared designer shell: map canvas (free / flow / both, grid, snap, rulers, guides, zoom) + layers tree on designerDoc with multi-select (click / ctrl / shift / marquee), drag within the tree and the map, panels placed by the designer interface (left / right / bottom / float / hidden)

Shared inspector from nodeProps (text, icon picker, action picker from rt.actions, view picker from the UI registry, bindings, choices, numbers) + root data fields from asset-types.json; the chrome settings dialog pattern for the designer interface (Settings…)

Shared context menu + keyboard: designerContextMenu entries (tip tooltips, disabled, submenus) on right-click / long-press of nodes and the canvas, DESIGNER_KEYS handling, clipboard (cut / copy / paste within and across designers), undo / redo on createHistory / commit with coalescing from the interface

Shared drag-and-drop in and out: parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop for palette items, assets from the library, actions, grid hooks (grid-hook@1), embeds, text, URLs and files; drop indicators (before / after / inside, map position); nodeDragPayload for dragging nodes out to other designers

Shared live preview: docked / floating / inline per the interface, desktop + phone frames, live or on-save refresh, through rt.swap on a preview id per type (never the app's real slot); AssetPreview miniature for the asset library cards

Save / publish flow: id suggestion + designedIdErrors, makeDesigned (origin = what Brett said when voice-started), version bump per the interface, library upsert, ui-registry.json declaration of the host (designedRegistryItem) + `ui-registry.mjs generate`, output target app / framework / hub, autosave

asset-context@1 in the runtime: contextExtras '*:asset' from data-axf-asset on every chrome, widget, dialog and embed element (Chrome.tsx, Widgets.tsx, TabGroup.tsx, Overlays.tsx carry the attribute), assetContextSection with the add-on in force, actions asset.preview / asset.about / asset.copyId / asset.usage registered, help@1 entries from assetInfo help-text

Menu rendering of the new entry fields: MenuList / Overlays draw tip (tooltip + Help mode), preview (a live miniature of the asset on hover: AssetPreview in a popover), disabled; About opens the hover card (phone: sheet) and the side panel; Where used lists hosts from the live chrome

App menu designer add-on: works inside the host (registered through the capability) and alone; help.json entries; 3+ preview options (desktop + phone shots) to UI Review (review.mjs submit --kind other --group "ui-asset-designer - <date>")

# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md
steps.why: new shared asset types + cross-port contract

steps.text: Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI
steps.why: library format + converter correctness is a contract every port reads

steps.text: Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections
steps.why: first consumer of the icon-library and icon-map contracts; shapes the plugin's data model

steps.text: Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group
steps.why: changes how GUIs work across apps (window / dock engine use, drag-drop between hosts)

steps.text: Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

steps.text: Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library
steps.why: forms and integrations on top of the contracts

steps.text: Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)
Polish: help.json for every control, menu-reach, help-coverage, check-theme / check-controls / check-chrome-assets / plugin-lifecycle / plugin-pages green; settings sections finished; console re-bake
Screenshots (desktop + phone) of at least 3 UI options for the browser and the manager submitted to UI Review; report _claude/builds/reports/icon-browser-manager.md; THREADS.md; PR opened and linked

before.title: skins-asset-types
before.detail: Upgrade skins to style every registry asset type (widgets, icon packs, composites, embeds, text blocks), scoped inheritance, registry-driven coverage + CI check. Brief: /root/axf-builds/skins-asset-types/.brief.md. Was queued directly; orchestrator to assign models.

origin.said: What about skins? How's skins doing? Is skins gonna um, be upgraded since we've we've made um so many more asset types? ... Added into skins.

addenda.said: Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry, not just the original kinds. Cover the new types: embeddable widget, icon pack, composite assets (button = box + text, nav = container + items), data set bar (search/filter/sort), embed, and every element down to text blocks/labels. Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance (same model as design/icon packs). A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack but doesn't have to. Pull the full asset-type list from the registry dynamically so new types are covered automatically going forward (no hardcoded list); add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.

steps.text: skin-coverage@1 engine: coverage of every registry type (slot / parts / reference / bundle / none) derived from asset-types.json, scope chain global → app → UI → plugin (child overrides parent), fixtures; registry declarations for the few types with no look

CI: check-skin-coverage fails on a registered type with no skin coverage; android.yml; rebake; typecheck; checks
